title: The Battle to Save General Donahue From Hegseth’s Army Purge
partialText: Gen. Christopher T. Donahue’s vision for fighting future wars won him powerful supporters around the world. Could they save his career?

title: How a Memphis Gambling Raid Became a Sweeping Immigration Operation
partialText: More than 120 people were arrested at a Memphis cantina, in one of the biggest immigration operations in Tennessee this year.

title: For Fired DeSantis Campaign Staff Member, a Second Chance at State Dept.
partialText: The hiring of Nate Hochman, who lost his job amid an uproar over a video containing a Nazi symbol, underscores the administration’s willingness to overlook past transgressions.

title: Trump Administration Again Asks Supreme Court to Allow Mail Voting Restrictions
partialText: The filing puts the legality of the president’s push to impose limits on mail voting squarely before the justices even as states begin sending out ballots.

title: Trump’s War on Mail-In Ballots Has Voters Baffled. That May Be the Point.
partialText: From Oregon to Florida, officials are at once reassuring voters that their ballots are safe and encouraging them to use drop boxes or vote in person.

title: New Hampshire Democrats Sound an Alarm: ‘We’re Losing’
partialText: The state has not elected a Republican to the Senate since 2010. But Chris Pappas, the likely Democratic nominee, anticipates a tough race against a well-known opponent, John E. Sununu.

title: As Midterms Approach, Republicans Find There Is No Escape From Trump
partialText: The president’s strategy, message and spending have left the G.O.P. in a difficult spot as lawmakers try to outrun his sagging approval ratings.

title: In Germany, Ulrich Siegmund Is Bringing the AfD to the Cusp of Power
partialText: Ulrich Siegmund, 35, once sold air fresheners. Now his far-right party is the favorite to win a state election in eastern Germany on Sunday.

title: In Ukraine, Fraud and Waste Are Rewarded With More Weapons Contracts
partialText: Secret military audits reveal a military procurement system riddled with mismanagement. In 2024 alone, Ukraine lost $1.2 billion to fraud and waste.

title: What Secret Audits Tell Us About How Ukraine’s Military Is Spending Its Money
partialText: The documents amount to an autopsy of the weapons-contracting process.

title: U.S. Envoys Witkoff and Kushner Arrive in Kyiv After Talks With Putin
partialText: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were meeting on Sunday with Volodymyr Zelensky in Ukraine, a day after talks with Vladimir V. Putin in Moscow.

title: Iran’s Attacks Keep the Strait of Hormuz in a Lethal Stalemate
partialText: The U.S. military is helping oil get out of the Persian Gulf on tankers, but Iran is still attacking the ships and scaring operators away.

title: OPEC Plus Holds Oil Production Steady as U.S.-Iran Strikes Resume
partialText: The decision on Sunday by the cartel of oil-producing nations and some of its allies came after the resumption of U.S. and Iranian military strikes in the Persian Gulf.

title: A Sympathetic Defendant and Well-Crafted Strategy Dominated Clancy Trial
partialText: The defense lawyer for Lindsay Clancy showed empathy for his client in showcasing her mental health problems. That may have made all the difference.

title: The 92-Year-Old Mathematician and the Teenage Apprentice
partialText: Joan Birman thought her major discoveries were behind her. Then came an email from a young neighbor — a girl who knew little but wanted to learn.

title: ‘Furious’ Is the First Thriller Made for a Post-Epstein World
partialText: “Furious,” the new police procedural on Hulu, turns out to be the perfect thriller for a post-Epstein world.

title: It’s Not Just the West Bank Settlers. It’s Israel.
partialText: Settler violence is reaching new heights.

title: Bummer Time
partialText: If you thought this summer felt a little bit off, you’re not alone.

title: How a Blacklisted Chinese Tech Giant Kept Buying America’s Best A.I. Chips
partialText: Washington imposed sanctions on Inspur because of its work with the Chinese military. But the company’s subsidiary kept shipping Nvidia’s best chips to feed China’s leading A.I. firms.
